question:
Narrow novelty check on TWO specific black-box model-fingerprinting features, for a prior-art gate that blocks a write-up.

WHY THIS GATE IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN ROUTINE. A previous gate (Aug 2026) cleared this research programme on exactly one ground: it found that generic black-box model identification is TAKEN (Model Equality Testing ICLR 2025; IRIS arXiv 2607.20860 at 0.99 verification AUROC), but that "iterated / dynamical probes are NOT anticipated -- every published feature set is single-shot scoring of supplied text", and concluded "pitch the novelty as the dynamics, not the fingerprint." The two features below are NOT iterated. Each is ONE forward pass on a two-token input. So they may have stepped off the only defensible ground the earlier gate identified, onto ground it said was already taken. That is the question.

THE MEASUREMENT, precisely. Take a language model's own next-token conditional p(. | x_{t-1}, x_t). Feed it the degenerate two-token input (t, t) -- the same token twice. Read the argmax. Two derived features:

(A) THE SELF-CONTINUATION SET. For every token t in the vocabulary, the bit: does argmax p(. | t, t) == t? This is asking whether the diagonal state (t,t) is a fixed point of the greedy/argmax map. The FEATURE is the whole bit-vector over ~50k tokens (or over a cross-tokenizer intersection of ~3.5k strings), not a count. Measured on 12 Pile-trained models in 4 families (Pythia, GPT-Neo, RWKV, Mamba). Also stored: the logit margin logit(t|t,t) - max_{x != t} logit(x|t,t).

(B) THE ESCAPE DESTINATION. For tokens where the bit is 0, the identity of argmax p(. | t, t) -- i.e. WHERE the map sends the state (t,t) when it does not stay. Compared across models as decoded STRINGS (token ids are not comparable across tokenizers). The estimand is the agreement rate between two models over shared source tokens. This gives leave-one-out rank-1 family attribution of 10/12 against a family-level chance of 22.7%.

QUESTIONS, and only these:

(a) Does any published work use a model's response to DEGENERATE or SELF-REFERENTIAL inputs (a token repeated, a token conditioned on itself, diagonal/identity inputs) as a black-box model fingerprint, watermark, or identity/provenance signal? This is the sharpest question -- not "model fingerprinting" generally, which is known to be taken, but this specific probe construction.

(b) Has anyone characterised the FIXED POINTS of greedy decoding (tokens that map to themselves under argmax of the model's own conditional) as a per-model property -- their number, their identity, or their set membership? Distinguish work that observes degenerate repetition loops as a FAILURE MODE (Holtzman et al. neural text degeneration, Fu et al. repetition, Xu et al. self-reinforcement) from work that uses fixed-point structure as an IDENTIFIER or a model-characterisation feature.

(c) The single-shot model-identification literature -- Model Equality Testing, IRIS, LLM fingerprinting, model provenance / IP protection, "which model is this API serving", TRAP, instructional fingerprinting, weight-free identification -- what INPUT CONSTRUCTIONS do these actually use? Do any of them probe with degenerate, out-of-distribution, or non-natural-language inputs rather than natural prompts or supplied text? Is a high-dimensional per-token bit-vector or per-token destination map used as the feature anywhere?

(d) Is there prior work on the ARGMAX MAP over token space as a dynamical object -- treating t -> argmax p(.|t,t) (or a windowed version) as a function on the vocabulary and studying its structure (fixed points, basins, where non-fixed tokens are sent)?

(e) Adjacent risk: work on "attractor" or "absorbing state" analysis of language model decoding; work on token-level transition graphs induced by greedy decoding; anything that builds a graph over the vocabulary from a model's own conditional.

VERDICT NEEDED: for feature (A) and feature (B) SEPARATELY -- novel, partially anticipated, or already taken? Name the 3-5 most threatening papers with citations and say exactly which part of which feature each would pre-empt. Also state explicitly whether the earlier gate's conclusion ("iterated/dynamical probes are the defensible ground") still protects these features, given that neither iterates.
summary: Neither feature is scooped outright, but the earlier gate's "dynamics" protection no longer covers them and the two features carry very different risk. Feature (A) is PARTIALLY ANTICIPATED: Hammouri et al. (SaTML 2025, arXiv:2410.06287) already probe with degenerate repeated-token inputs, already formalise the temperature-0 argmax fixed-point condition, already report a per-token x per-model matrix and lineage inheritance of fixed points — everything except the vocabulary-wide bit-vector and the identifier use. Feature (B) is the stronger claim and survives as NOVEL IN CONSTRUCTION: no published work records where the argmax map sends non-fixed degenerate states (Hammouri explicitly logs those failures as the integer 0), but (B)'s comparison metric (cross-model agreement rate) and its evaluation protocol (leave-one-out family attribution against a chance rate from a fixed single-shot probe battery) are both already published, so its novelty rests entirely on the input construction and the vocabulary index set. The binding constraint on both is self-prior-art, not third parties: this project's own paper 1 (arXiv:2608.10986) already publishes the argmax map as a dynamical object, the per-model fixed-point/dispersion contrast, and — in the public findings record it cites — the literal diagonal probe argmax(x | t,t) == t on named models, while its related-work section asserts on the record that single-shot feature sets are the taken ground. Practical verdict: both features are writable, but only with an explicit delta paragraph against arXiv:2410.06287 and against paper 1, and with the novelty pitched as the vocabulary-wide set-valued destination map, not as "degenerate probes" or "fixed points" per se.

findings.claim: THE TOP EXTERNAL THREAT TO FEATURE (A) is Hammouri, Derya & Sunar, "Non-Halting Queries: Exploiting Fixed Points in LLMs" (IEEE SaTML 2025). It probes with degenerate repeated-token inputs, formalises the temperature-0 argmax fixed-point condition, reports per-model rates over a 100-token sample, publishes a per-token x per-model matrix, and observes that fixed points are inherited across model lineages. It pre-empts the OBSERVATION and the PROBE SHAPE behind (A) — but not the vocabulary-wide bit-vector, not the escape destination, and not any identification use.
findings.vote: 4 merged claims, votes 2-1, 3-0, 3-0, 3-0; all verified against the full v2 PDF, not the abstract
findings.evidence: Verbatim from the paper: "We repeated this experiment for single token inputs with words like 'John' or 'Adam' and observed that a repetition of 3 times to form the cycle-pattern (a total of 3 input tokens) was sufficient to send the model into a non-halting cyclic anomaly" (Fig. 3 shows base Meta-Llama-3-8B on input 'JohnJohnJohn'). Its formalism is literally the fixed-point condition: at temperature 0 "any fixed point x of f such that f(x1,x2,x3) = x1,x2,x3 gives us a non-halting anomaly" — T=0 is argmax, so this is argmax p(.|t,t,t)=t. Title and index terms are "Fixed Points". Sec. V-E reports per-model success over 100 random words (ChatGPT-4o 97%, Llama-3.1-8B 97%, Gemma-2-9B 91%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 44%, Gemini-1.5-Pro 19%), and Appendix D Tables IV/V give a 100-word x 5-model matrix of per-token repetition counts with 0 = failure. It also states fixed points are lineage-inherited: "once we identify a cycle in the base model for some LLM, we may transfer the same cycle to target a different aligned model" — the same invariance feature (B)'s family attribution rests on. THE GAPS THAT SURVIVE: minimal construction is (t,t,t)/3 tokens over a windowed context settled by multi-step generation, not one forward pass on the 2-token diagonal; no vocabulary sweep ("vocabulary" appears once, unrelated); no logit margin; no bit-vector; per-model statistic is a scalar success rate ranking attack difficulty, and Table I entangles alignment refusal with the underlying map because it attacks aligned chat models through an instruction wrapper with up to 1000 repetitions.

findings.claim: FEATURE (B)'s CORE OBSERVABLE — the identity of argmax p(.|t,t) for tokens that are NOT fixed points — is recorded nowhere in the prior art. Hammouri et al. explicitly discard non-cycling tokens with no record of what the model emitted instead; Yona et al. never read a next-token distribution at all; Fu et al. never expose a per-token quantity; and paper 1 reports gpt2-medium's dispersion only as a COUNT of endpoints. No paper decodes escape destinations as strings or compares them across models.
findings.vote: claim [4] 3-0 plus corroborating negative sweeps inside claims [2], [3], [8], [9], [10], [12]
findings.evidence: Hammouri Sec. V-E, verbatim: "Any prompt that does not result in a non-halting query using the maximum number of repetitions is considered to have failed and we move to the next token." Appendix D makes the discard literal: "A zero means the model does not produce a non-halting response for the corresponding word." Full-text negative sweeps of that paper return zero hits for argmax, decoded, destination, basin, attractor, graph, cross-model, fingerprint, provenance, attribut*, agreement; the only two "escape" hits are a scalar logprob trajectory inside an already-successful run and "escape alignment". Yona et al. (ICML 2025) returns zero hits for argmax/greedy/logit/top-1/sampling — every observable is a white-box hidden-state norm or a zero-ablation. Fu et al. (AAAI 2021) exposes only the scalar trace ARP = sum_k tr(B^2k / (zeta^k n^k)); no token is ever reported as a self-successor. Xu et al. (NeurIPS 2022) averages its Winner Rate into a scalar over one model. The single-shot fingerprinting line indexes features by QUERY or by RESPONSE, never by vocabulary token.

findings.claim: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON BOTH FEATURES IS SELF-PRIOR-ART. This project's own paper 1 (arXiv:2608.10986, cs.CL, 11 Aug 2026) already treats x -> argmax p_r as a dynamical object over token space, already reports its per-model fixed-point structure as a distinguishing contrast, and already gestures at where non-fixed states go; the public findings record it cites contains the exact diagonal probe argmax(x | t,t) == t. Feature (A)'s per-token bit on the 2-token diagonal is therefore already in print at small scale, on named models.
findings.vote: claim [6] 2-1; two stronger versions of this claim were REFUTED 0-3, so the overlap is conceptual/mechanistic, not the full estimand; verified against the arXiv PDF and the local sources of record
findings.evidence:
main.tex:297-303 (published verbatim, confirmed by pdftotext on the arXiv PDF): "The mechanism is an attracting fixed point of the argmax map. At T = 0.02 the update is essentially deterministic, so the dynamics are governed by the map x -> arg max p_r. For pythia-410m this map sends 18 of 24 random starts to the newline token --- a genuine fixed point. For gpt2-medium it has no such point and wanders to 11 distinct endpoints." findings.md:2323 and :2326 record the non-iterated diagonal directly: "argmax(x | '
','
') == '
' FIXED POINT" and "argmax(x | ' the',' the') != ' the' NO FIXED POINT". WHAT IS NOT PRE-EMPTED (and why the stronger claims were refuted): a term census over the published full text returns 0 hits for fingerprint, provenance, escape, destination, basin, diagonal, self-continuation, bit-vector; gpt2's endpoints are a count, never per-token identities; scale is 24 starts x 2 models vs ~50k tokens x 12 models; and there is no cross-model agreement rate or LOO attribution. An earlier gate in this repo reached the same conclusion independently — results/prior_art_paper3_gate.json calls self-prior-art "the biggest single cut in this gate", noting web verifiers refuted all four claims on this ID 0-3 before it was overturned by direct inspection of the local source of record. A reviewer cannot call this a scoop, but can call it unacknowledged self-overlap if the delta is left unstated.

findings.claim: FEATURE (B)'s COMPARISON STATISTIC IS STANDARD, NOT NOVEL. The "agreement rate between two models over shared source tokens" is the established estimand of the model-provenance line: Stemma's A(S,T) is the fraction of probe-permutation observations preserving the source decision, Model Provenance Testing measures NEXT-TOKEN agreement between source and suspect, and IPGuard/Tang et al. use the same match-rate form. Any novelty in (B) must rest on the probe construction and index set, never on the metric.
findings.vote: claim [5] 3-0, verified against Stemma's Eq. (7) in the PDF; over-determined by three independent method lineages
findings.evidence: Stemma (Zhang, Safronov, Martin; Oxford; 28 Jul 2026) Sec. 4.4 Eq. (7): A(S,T) = (1/KC) sum_{(q,h_S(q)) in F_S} sum_{pi in Pi(q)} 1[d_T(q,pi) = h_S(q)], glossed by the authors as "the fraction of the KC probe-permutation observations that preserve the source region assignment". The likeliest refutation (that Stemma's real statistic is the log-probability margin) was tested and failed: the margin is a source-side probe-eligibility filter, and A(S,T) is the score fed to AUC. Stemma's own related work states that Model Provenance Testing (Nikolic et al., NeurIPS 2025) "measures next-token agreement between the source and suspect relative to independently trained control models" — an even tighter match to (B), since MPT's decision space IS the next token. Imprecision noted by the verifier: Stemma's statistic is asymmetric over a 4-way decision space with permutation replicates, so "structurally identical statistic" is more accurate than "same estimand"; the concession stands regardless via MPT.

findings.claim: FEATURE (B)'s EVALUATION PROTOCOL IS ALSO PUBLISHED, from a NON-ITERATED single-forward-pass probe: "One Token Is Enough" (Bruckner, 11 Jul 2026) runs a fixed probe battery, collects one output token per query black-box, computes cross-model divergence, and reports leave-one-out nearest-neighbour FAMILY attribution against a chance rate — 59.5% vs 18.4% over 163 models, plus 7.3% EER over 165 models. That is the same experimental design as (B)'s 10/12 LOO vs 22.7% chance. What it does NOT anticipate is the feature representation: its index set is (task, language), a 40-cell battery of natural-language prompts, never the vocabulary.
findings.vote: the FEATURE-REPRESENTATION half is claim [0], 3-0, verified against the full HTML text; the PROTOCOL half survives only as the verifier's scope caveat because both a clearing claim and a threatening claim about this paper were refuted 0-3
findings.evidence: Verbatim: "The fingerprint of M is the tuple F(M) = (p_hat^M_{t,l})_{(t,l) in B}", where B is "ten tasks in four languages (English, Russian, Chinese, Arabic): random and favorite numbers, random letters, words, colors, animals, cities, and a coin flip", compared by mean Jensen-Shannon divergence over cells (Eq. 1). Attribution protocol, Sec. IV-C: "classify each model's family by its nearest neighbor, leave-one-out"; abstract: "59.5% leave-one-out accuracy against an 18.4% chance rate". No logits, no per-token bit-vector, no destination map, no degenerate input anywhere; its stated design principle is "we instead optimize what to measure" versus LLMmap/TRAP's optimisation of what to send. The temperature-0 variant it collects is used only as a serving-stack stability diagnostic ("At temperature 0, 90.4% of cells are deterministic within serving provider"), never as a cross-model attribution feature — so it is not a destination map. Caution: the verifiers refused BOTH the claim that this paper leaves the probe construction clear AND the claim that it materially damages the earlier gate's premise, so treat the protocol overlap as documented-but-contested rather than settled.

findings.claim: THE DEGENERATION / REPETITION LITERATURE SITS ENTIRELY ON THE FAILURE-MODE SIDE and pre-empts no identifier use — but it contains two real conceptual ancestors that the write-up must not overclaim past: Xu et al.'s "Winner Rate" is an argmax-fixed-point indicator on repeated content, and Fu et al. explicitly note that greedy decoding makes next-word prediction a deterministic function on the vocabulary. Yona et al.'s repeated-token work is white-box, long-repetition, and further from (A) than either.
findings.vote: claims [7] 3-0, [8] 3-0, [9] 3-0, [10] 2-1, [11] 2-1, [12] 2-1; all verified against full PDFs
findings.evidence: Fu et al. (AAAI 2021), verbatim: "In greedy sampling, each word only takes a fixed subsequent word and thus zeta_n = 1" — i.e. the transition matrix becomes the adjacency matrix of a function V -> V. But their B is a corpus bigram count matrix, not the model's own conditional, and the only diagonal object is B^k_ii folded into a scalar trace; zero hits for fixed point, attractor, fingerprint, provenance. They ARE a live partial hit on question (e): they build a vocabulary transition graph with named structural quantities (sparsity = mean out-degree, "inflow" = in-degree mass, "outflow"). Xu et al. (NeurIPS 2022) define WR(s^n) = (1/L_s) sum_l 1(x_{n,l} is a winner) where a winner requires "x_{n,l} = arg max P(.|x_{<n,l})" — the same object as (A)'s bit, but on multi-token sentences, averaged to a scalar, one 750M model, framed as degeneration. Their Sec. 2 probe corpus D_random is explicitly out-of-distribution — "the tokens of sentences are randomly sampled from the vocabulary of the model" — so "nobody has fed a model non-natural input and read its own continuation" would be an overstatement. Yona et al. (ICML 2025) is white-box only (zero hits for argmax/greedy/logit/sampling), needs 450-4000 repetitions to induce a sink, and logs per-token variation as an unexplained limitation: "Not all tokens in LLaMa2 induce sinks (see Figure 6), suggesting other factors are at play." All three: zero occurrences of fingerprint, provenance, watermark, attribution.

findings.claim: THE EARLIER GATE'S DEFENCE ("pitch the novelty as the dynamics, not the fingerprint") NO LONGER PROTECTS THESE FEATURES AS WRITTEN. Paper 1 itself put in print the assertion that single-shot feature sets are what the identification literature already does, and both features are one forward pass. The salvageable reframing is that the OBJECT measured is dynamical (fixed points and destinations of the argmax map) even though the MEASUREMENT is single-shot — but that reframing runs straight into paper 1, which already banked exactly that object.
findings.vote: the strong form ("cannot inherit the dynamics defence") was REFUTED 0-3; the weaker form here is supported by claim [6]'s verifier evidence and by direct inspection of main.tex
findings.evidence: main.tex:747-749, published verbatim: "in the model-identification literature specifically, every published feature set performs single-shot scoring of supplied text rather than measuring dynamics at all" — the sentence that stakes paper 1's novelty on dynamics. The same section concedes "We do not claim the observation that iteration has attractors", locating paper 1's contribution in the measurement (damage spreading with an exact-zero null, Lyapunov exponent, damping length). Features (A) and (B) do not iterate, so by paper 1's own framing they fall on the single-shot side. The refutation of the strong form is worth respecting: measuring a fixed point of a map is a dynamical-systems question regardless of iteration count, so a reviewer need not accept that the features are "merely" single-shot. But that argument buys ground already occupied by paper 1, not new ground.

findings.claim: VERDICT ON FEATURE (A) — SELF-CONTINUATION BIT-VECTOR: PARTIALLY ANTICIPATED. The probe shape, the fixed-point framing, the per-token/per-model tabulation and the lineage inheritance are all in Hammouri et al.; the exact 2-token diagonal bit is in this project's own paper-1 record. What survives as new: the exhaustive vocabulary sweep (~50k tokens, ~3.5k cross-tokenizer intersection), the SET-VALUED feature (which tokens, not how many), the stored logit margin, and the use as an identity signal. Do not pitch (A) as "degenerate probes" or "fixed points of greedy decoding" — both are taken.
findings.vote: synthesis of claims [1],[2],[3],[4],[6],[10],[12]; the four Hammouri claims verified 2-1/3-0/3-0/3-0 against the full PDF
findings.evidence: Nearest published objects, ranked by threat: (1) Hammouri Appendix D Tables IV/V — a 100-word x 5-model matrix of per-token behaviour with 0 = failure, one aggregation step away from (A), plus per-model rates 97%..19% and "a simple recipe that takes the same fixed points observed in the base model"; (2) paper 1's findings record, argmax(x | t,t) == t on pythia-410m and gpt2-medium — the identical construction at n=2 models; (3) Xu et al.'s Winner Rate, an argmax-fixed-point indicator collapsed to a scalar; (4) Fu et al.'s zeta_n = 1, greedy as a deterministic vocabulary map. None of the four is a vocabulary-indexed bit-vector, none stores a logit margin, and none uses the structure to identify a model.

findings.claim: VERDICT ON FEATURE (B) — ESCAPE DESTINATION MAP: NOVEL, BUT NARROW AND SURROUNDED. The observable itself is genuinely unoccupied — no published work records where the argmax map sends a non-fixed degenerate state, and the one paper that could have (Hammouri) throws that information away as a zero. But the metric is standard (Stemma / MPT agreement rate), the protocol is published (One Token Is Enough LOO family attribution vs chance), and the underlying "where does the map send non-fixed states" idea appears in paper 1's dispersion count. The claimable delta is exactly: the input construction (the (t,t) diagonal) crossed with the vocabulary index set, read as decoded strings for cross-tokenizer comparability.
findings.vote: synthesis of claims [0],[4],[5],[6]; the untouched-observable finding is 3-0, the metric-is-standard finding is 3-0
findings.evidence: (B) is the stronger of the two features: the four papers that come closest each miss it on a different axis — Hammouri never records the destination, Stemma/MPT supply the statistic but probe with natural-language multiple-choice or selected queries over a 4-way or next-token decision space, Bruckner supplies the LOO-vs-chance protocol but indexes by (task, language), and paper 1 reports gpt2-medium's "11 distinct endpoints" as a count with zero hits for destination/escape/basin. The cross-tokenizer decoded-string agreement rate over shared source tokens, and its 10/12 LOO family attribution against 22.7% chance, are not pre-empted as a feature — though the claim SHAPE (LOO family attribution beating chance from a black-box probe battery) demonstrably is.

verdicts.F95_dynamics_defence: NO LONGER PROTECTS these features as written
